server.name: repoctl
server.title: repoctl package set builder
server.toolPolicy: repoctl mcp start --tools read|all|NAME,... A tool that is not in the mode is not listed by tools/list and a call fails with the problem mcp.tool-not-allowed (isError true). The web UI starts its agent with --tools read.
server.upgradePolicy: Before each tool call, the server checks its own executable. When a dnf upgrade replaced it, each call fails with the problem host.stale-server (exit 9, isError true). The human restarts the agent session.

tools.name: repoctl_status
tools.title: Set status
tools.description: Show the package set in the current directory: targets (active or retired), lock state of each package (in-sync, in-tree, ahead, behind, diverged, dirty, missing, unpinned, orphaned), the holder of the set lock, the active run, the last run, and for each target the snapshot latest in the registry, the local copy (same, behind, unpushed, none) and the HTTP server (same, behind, unknown, with the heartbeat of the mirror job and the warning served.stale). It counts the nodes in flight: pinned, not in latest, staged here or to build here. It lists the steps of new-set and onboarding that are not done. Call this first in a new session. Returns kind Status.

tools.name: repoctl_doctor
tools.title: Check the build host
tools.description: Check that this host can build the set and publish: mock group membership, mock configs of each target, rpmautospec plugin, the signing key and its deployment record (sign.*), createrepo_c, disk space, XDG directories, the registry login and scope (registry.*), the daily check (check.*), reachability of external git URLs, the key of the tool repository (tool.repo-key), servers that an upgrade left behind (host.stale-server), that git signs commits with the signing key (git.signing), the GitHub rulesets of the set repository (git.protection), that the installed skills match the binary, and that the guard hook covers the set (skills.guard). Each check is ok, warning or failed, with a remediation line. A missing secret key is only a warning on a host that builds. Use it when a build fails before the srpm step. Returns kind DoctorReport.

tools.name: repoctl_show
tools.title: Show packages
tools.description: Show packages of the set: source branch or external URL, locked commit, worktree HEAD and state, per target the NVR, dependencies, dependents, published build and plan action, version and release per target, upstream settings and the notes from repoctl.yaml. Read the notes before you propose a version change: they hold rules such as 'upstream 4.x is frozen'. Returns kind Package, one item per package. Maps to repoctl list (all) and repoctl show <package>.

packages.description: Packages, e.g. ["ucx"]. Empty or absent: all packages.

tools.name: repoctl_graph
tools.title: Build graph
tools.description: Return the dependency graph of each target. An edge from A to B means A must be built before B; via lists the BuildRequires that matched. unresolved lists requires that only a node of another target provides: these often cause a builddep failure. Returns kind Graph, one item per target.

targets.description: Target ids, e.g. ["el10"]. Absent: all targets.

tools.name: repoctl_plan
tools.title: Plan a build
tools.description: Show what a build would do and why, without building. Each node gets action build, current (the commit is in latest), staged (built for this lock, not published) or skip. A build node lists reasons with a code: commit-changed, rebuild, new-package, new-target, forced or staging-missing (the staging of a staged node is gone). repoctl never rebuilds a dependent by itself: read plan.advisories (for example provider.changed) to see which dependents may need repoctl_rebuild. Read warnings: dep.not-for-target predicts a builddep failure. A selected worktree that is not in-sync with repoctl.lock gives the error lock.dirty, as repoctl_build does; the plan still has all nodes. The first plan of a target can take minutes because repoctl builds SRPMs to read their requires. Returns kind Plan.

packages.description: Limit to these packages. Absent: all.

force.description: Plan the selected nodes as build even if current or staged (reason forced).

from.description: lock: pinned commits. worktree: worktree HEAD commits, as repoctl_build with from worktree.

withDeps.description: Also select the transitive dependencies of packages.

rdeps.description: Also select the packages that depend on packages.

check.description: repoctl plan --check: _meta repoctl/exitCode is 11 when a node has the action build.

tools.name: repoctl_upstream
tools.title: Upstream versions
tools.description: Compare each package version with the latest upstream release (GitHub tags or releases with the tag filter from repoctl.yaml, and the Fedora rawhide version). status is up-to-date, update-available, ahead, frozen (the notes say so) or unknown. newer lists the tags between the current and the latest version; use releaseNotesUrl to read what changed. Answers are cached for one hour unless refresh is true. Returns kind Upstream.

tools.name: repoctl_runs
tools.title: Run history
tools.description: List recent build, publish, check and gc runs of the set, newest first, with state and node counts. Use it to find the run id of the last failed build. Returns kind Run with nodes left empty; call repoctl_run_get for the nodes.

tools.name: repoctl_run_get
tools.title: Run details
tools.description: Return one run with every node: state (waiting, running, ok, failed, blocked, canceled), steps with durations and exit codes, NVRs, artifacts, log paths, and for a failed node an error with class and a log excerpt. Works while the run is in progress. publishable lists targets that a human may publish (every node current or staged); publishBlockers says why the others are not. next lists suggested steps; a step with human: true is for the human only. Returns kind Run.

artifacts.description: Include the artifact list of each node (file, path, size, sha256). Absent: NVRs only.

tools.name: repoctl_run_wait
tools.title: Wait for a run
tools.description: Wait until a run ends or timeoutSeconds pass, then return the run as repoctl_run_get does. Sends MCP progress notifications (nodes ended of build nodes, from the journal) when the call has a progressToken. If the run is not done when the time ends, call the tool again. Do not poll faster: one call can wait up to 600 seconds. If the process of the run ended without a result, the call returns at once with state abandoned and the error run.abandoned; the open nodes count as canceled.

artifacts.description: Include the artifact list of each node (file, path, size, sha256). Absent: NVRs only.

tools.name: repoctl_logs
tools.title: Node log
tools.description: Return lines of the log of one node in a run (repoctl logs RUN NODE). By default it returns the error excerpt and the last 120 lines of the node log (all steps: srpm, rpm, stage). file selects one mock log instead. Use grep to find a pattern such as error: or Failed build dependencies. Returns kind NodeLog; lines are escaped and each line is cut at 2000 bytes.

run.description: Run id. Absent: the newest run that has this node.

file.description: repoctl: the node log (default). root, build, state: the mock log of the failed or last step.

grep.description: RE2 regular expression; returns matching lines with 3 lines of context, at most 400 lines.

tools.name: repoctl_repo_ls
tools.title: Repo contents
tools.description: List the RPMs in the local copy of latest, in a snapshot, or in the staging repo of a run. One item per target and repo (slurm, slurm-source, slurm-debuginfo). Returns kind RepoContents.

run.description: Staging repo of this run. Absent: the local copy of latest.

name.description: Glob on the package name, e.g. slurm-*.

snapshot.description: A publish id or digest. The server reads the manifest from the registry.

removed.description: List removed[] of the RepoManifest: each NVR that a prune or a restore removed, with the publish and the reason.

tools.name: repoctl_repo_diff
tools.title: Staging vs published
tools.description: Compare the staging repo of a run (or the staged nodes of the plan) with the local copy of latest: added, removed, changed (other EVR) and rebuilt (same NVRA, other payload). Use it to write the summary a human reads before they publish. Returns kind RepoDiff, one item per target and repo.

tools.name: repoctl_repo_verify
tools.title: Verify repositories
tools.description: Verify the signatures and checksums of a repository: the local copy of latest by default, a snapshot, the served tree, or the staging repo of a run. With el, also install-test the repodata in the EL mock chroot. Returns kind DoctorReport (one check per repository).

tools.name: repoctl_repo_provenance
tools.title: Provenance of a build
tools.description: Show the SLSA provenance record of one build: commit, run, builder, subjects, source archives and the buildroot changes since the previous build of the same package. The default source is the local copy of latest. Use it to answer how an RPM was built, or which builds used a buildroot package. Returns kind Provenance.

build.description: An NVR, or PKG@TARGET for the newest build of that node.

snapshot.description: A publish id or digest. The server reads the record from the registry.

tools.name: repoctl_repo_sbom
tools.title: SBOM of a target or a build
tools.description: Show the CycloneDX SBOM of each target, or of one build: components, purls, versions, licenses. Use it to find the RPMs that hold an upstream version, for example for a CVE. Returns kind Sbom, one item per target or one for the build.

tools.name: repoctl_snapshots
tools.title: List snapshots
tools.description: List the snapshots of each target in the registry, newest first, with publish id, digest, parent, kind, signer, human and host. Use it to find the publish that changed an NVR. With history, it also lists the snapshots that gc deleted. Returns kind SnapshotList, one item per target.

all.description: Also list the tags that are not on the parent chain of latest, for example a publish that diverged or lost the tag race (repo snapshots --all).

history.description: List the publish history of latest: each publish of the chain, also snapshots that gc deleted, with the acceptances and their reasons and the trust changes.

tools.name: repoctl_advisories
tools.title: List advisories
tools.description: List the advisories of the last check and of each run that has staged nodes. level required blocks the publish of its closure; warn and info do not. dismissed includes dismissed and stale entries. refresh runs repoctl check first. Returns kind AdvisoryList.

tools.name: repoctl_advisory
tools.title: Show one advisory
tools.description: Show one advisory: level, state, facts, the closure, the suggested command and the dismissal. Use it to decide whether a rebuild is necessary. Returns kind Advisory.

tools.name: repoctl_check
tools.title: Check for advisories
tools.description: Run the read-only check of the set: closure checks against latest, provider changes, upstream releases, mock and buildroot drift, retired packages that are still published, signer keys that expire inside the warn window. It writes only check.json in the state dir. A narrowed check replaces only the results of its codes and targets; a failed code keeps its last good advisories (carriedFrom). Returns kind AdvisoryList.

codes.description: Advisory codes to check, e.g. closure.broken. Absent: all codes. The same as repoctl check --code.

tools.name: repoctl_sign_ls
tools.title: List signing keys
tools.description: List the keys of sign.keys with state (active, retiring, removed, revoked), the deployment and removal records, the expiry and the number of RPMs in latest that each key signed. deployed is true when each target in scope with a latest has a record. Returns kind SignerList.

targets.description: Target ids or globs. Default: all targets of the set.

tools.name: repoctl_sign_onboard
tools.title: Onboarding checklist for a key
tools.description: Check the five onboarding steps of one key: the key is in sign.keys, the key file holds it, a release with the key is published, the deployment is recorded, and the human has write access to the registry. It only prints and checks. Returns kind OnboardReport.

tools.name: repoctl_sign_offboard
tools.title: Offboarding checklist for a key
tools.description: Check the six offboarding steps of one key: the GitHub team, state retiring, the re-sign of its RPMs per target, state removed, a release without the key per target, and the removal record per target. clientCommands holds the commands that config management runs on the clients. It only prints and checks. Returns kind OnboardReport.

targets.description: Target ids or globs. Default: all targets of the set.

tools.name: repoctl_sign_keyfile
tools.title: Key file of latest
tools.description: Return the key file in latest of each target (the root key file of the snapshot), or with checksum its sha256: the pin of the client bootstrap. With tree, read the key file of the in-tree release package, which can be ahead of latest. Returns kind File.

targets.description: Target ids or globs. Default: all targets of the set.

tools.name: repoctl_config_show
tools.title: Show configuration
tools.description: Show each configuration value and where it came from (flag, env, user config, set, default). Returns kind Config.

key.description: Limit to keys with this prefix, e.g. sign.

tools.name: repoctl_schema
tools.title: Print a JSON Schema
tools.description: Print the JSON Schema of repoctl.yaml (config), of the --json output (output) or of the run journal (events). The result is the schema document, not an envelope.

tools.name: repoctl_build
tools.title: Build to staging
tools.description: Start a build of the set into the staging repo and return when the plan is ready, with the run id. Only nodes with action build run; current and staged nodes are not built again. It never signs and never publishes. It never builds uncommitted files: a dirty worktree fails with code lock.dirty and a humanAction. With from=lock (default), every selected worktree must match repoctl.lock (else lock.dirty). There is no build queue: when another build of this user runs on this host, the call fails with code set.busy and names that run; wait for it with repoctl_run_wait. Follow the new run with repoctl_run_wait. Returns kind Run (state planning or running).

packages.description: Build these packages. Needed dependencies that are not current or staged are added. Absent: all.

force.description: Build the selected nodes again (reason forced), for tests. A forced build of a current node is never staged or published.

from.description: lock: pinned commits (publishable). worktree: worktree HEAD commits, to try a commit before pin; the run is never publishable, and its nodes are never staged.

failFast.description: Stop after the first failure. Default: keep going with independent nodes.

withDeps.description: Also select the transitive dependencies of packages. It changes the result only with force.

rdeps.description: Also build the packages that depend on packages.

tools.name: repoctl_run_cancel
tools.title: Cancel a run
tools.description: Cancel a build run that this MCP server started (repoctl cancel): origin.via is mcp and origin.session is the session id of this server. Running nodes are stopped, waiting nodes end canceled, the staging repo keeps the nodes that ended ok. A run started from the CLI, the web UI, another MCP session or by another user is not canceled: the call fails with code cancel.foreign-run and a humanAction. After this server stops, only the human can cancel its runs.

force.description: repoctl cancel --force: kill the mock children at once, as a second Ctrl-C does. Use it only when the run stays interrupting.

tools.name: repoctl_checkout
tools.title: Check out locked commits
tools.description: Create or update package worktrees at the commits in repoctl.lock, and fetch the clones of external packages. Each worktree is attached to its local branch (the branch of the package entry); checkout moves a local branch only forward. It never discards changes: a dirty worktree or a worktree with commits that are not in the lock stays as it is, with a row and the warning worktree.dirty (exit 0, as in the CLI). With more than one package it continues after a failed package and exits 1. With create, it makes a new package branch from the source that you name (fromSet, from or orphan). It never pushes; the result names the push command. Returns kind Lock.

create.description: Create the package branch of each package from the start point that you name.

from.description: create: start the branch from this branch, or fedora.

fromSet.description: create: start each branch from the same package branch of this set branch.

tools.name: repoctl_pin
tools.title: Pin worktree commits
tools.description: Write the HEAD commit of the named package worktrees into repoctl.lock. Use it after you commit a spec change in packages/<package>. It does not commit repoctl.lock and does not push. It writes a line only when the worktree is ahead of it or the package is unpinned. It refuses a dirty worktree (code lock.dirty, with a humanAction), a diverged worktree (lock.diverged) and a worktree that is behind the lock (lock.behind: run repoctl_checkout; an agent never pins an older commit). When one package is refused, it writes nothing. It warns when the commit is not on the remote (lock.unpushed). Returns kind Lock with previous and new commits.

tools.name: repoctl_rebuild
tools.title: Rebuild with a new release
tools.description: Make an empty commit in the package branch so that rpmautospec raises the release, and let the next plan show the reason rebuild. Use it when an advisory says that a dependent needs a rebuild, or when the build must run again for the same version. It pins the new commit in repoctl.lock, as repoctl rebuild does. It does not push and does not build: the result names the push command and the commit of repoctl.lock. It refuses a worktree that is not in-sync (lock.dirty) and an in-tree package (rebuild.in-tree): to build an in-tree package again, the human changes a file below its path. It checks every package before the first commit: when one package fails, it makes no commit. Returns kind Lock.

reason.description: Goes into the commit message and the plan reason.
